items.headline: Workers' Party proposes an NTU-anchored R&D 'growth zone' in economy debate
items.summary: In a parliamentary motion on the future economy seconded by MP Jamus Lim, the Workers' Party proposed a research district zoned around Nanyang Technological University, run by its own authority that could take equity in the firms it grows. The PAP rebutted that local SMEs succeed because of ties with multinationals, not in spite of them.

items.headline: Singapore firm and three people charged over faking origin of goods sent to US
items.summary: Singapore Customs charged a company and three individuals for allegedly declaring China-origin goods as Singapore-made in about S$1.9 million of exports to the United States between August 2024 and September 2025, and for evading roughly S$111,000 in GST by understating import values. False declaration carries up to a S$10,000 fine and two years' jail.

items.headline: Chinese national jailed three years eight months for a Singapore housebreaking spree
items.summary: Huang Xiaozong, 41, was sentenced on Aug 14 to three years and eight months' jail after pleading guilty to two housebreaking charges. He entered Singapore on Dec 5, 2025, targeted homes in wealthier neighbourhoods and stole about S$105,750 in cash and valuables before his arrest three days later.

items.headline: Maid jailed after grabbing 94-year-old employer's cane, causing a fall and head injury
items.summary: Domestic helper Sulastri Wulandari, 31, pleaded guilty on Aug 14 to causing hurt and was sentenced the same day. Her 94-year-old employer fell and hit his head after she took away his walking cane when he asked her to prepare food.

items.headline: Football chiefs back anti-scalping drive as Singapore-Thailand tickets resold for S$1,500
items.summary: Ahead of the ASEAN Championship semi-final against Thailand at Jalan Besar Stadium, more than 4,000 home tickets priced from about S$24 sold out within minutes and reappeared on resale sites for up to S$1,500 a pair. Head coach Gavin Lee and captain Irfan Fandi urged fans to shun scalpers.

items.headline: Modi's 80th Independence Day speech pledges AI skilling for 10 million youth
items.summary: In his 13th consecutive Red Fort address, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced AI training for one crore (10 million) young people over the next year, urged all parties to back 33% reservation for women in legislatures, and launched a nationwide sports talent hunt for children aged 5 to 15. He framed the measures around a 'Viksit Bharat 2047' roadmap.

items.headline: Flash floods and a landslide kill four in Arunachal Pradesh; five soldiers missing
items.summary: Heavy rain on Aug 14 sent a flash flood through the 5th Grenadier's Pasu Pani Army camp in Dibang Valley, sweeping away seven personnel; two were rescued and five remain missing. A separate landslide at a road-cutting site in Upper Subansiri killed four construction workers as ITBP, GREF and state teams searched the debris.

items.headline: India name Harmanpreet-led Women's Asia Cup squad; Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out injured
items.summary: The BCCI named a 15-member squad captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, with Smriti Mandhana as deputy, for the Women's T20 Asia Cup in Dubai from Aug 28. Jemimah Rodrigues was ruled out with a high-grade hamstring tear suffered in The Hundred, and Pratika Rawal was named as her replacement.

items.headline: NHS England waiting list climbs to 7.4 million, its worst level since March
items.summary: The number of treatments waiting to be carried out in England rose by about 34,000 in July to roughly 7.4 million, with just 61.3% completed within the 18-week target. Surgeons pressed ministers for operating-theatre funding in the autumn budget as strike disruption weighed on the figures.

items.headline: UK heatwave hits 34.7C as hosepipe bans reach millions of households
items.summary: Temperatures peaked at 34.7C during the latest heatwave, with 33 days above 30C so far this summer, one short of the 1995 record. Hosepipe bans imposed by Thames Water and South West Water now cover roughly 15 million people.

items.headline: RMT strike disrupts East Midlands Railway services on Saturday
items.summary: An RMT walkout cut East Midlands Railway to about one train an hour on its main London St Pancras routes on Aug 15, with a reduced timetable running only between 07:00 and 19:00. The union is in dispute over the operator's refusal to withdraw a fleet of faulty trains.

items.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Indonesia's Flores coast kills at least 47
items.summary: A magnitude 7.7 quake struck at 5:58am on Aug 15 about 68km north-northwest of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara, at a depth of 10km. At least 47 people were killed and dozens injured; a tsunami warning was issued then lifted, and authorities recorded more than 235 aftershocks as landslides cut off remote villages.

items.headline: Update: Israeli strikes kill 11 in south Lebanon as UAE reports third Hormuz tanker hit
items.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 11 people, including a Hezbollah commander and children, while the UAE again accused Iran of attacking an ADNOC-owned tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, the third such strike in a week. Iran-backed Houthis also renewed attacks on a Yemeni Red Sea port.

items.headline: US carrier fleet stretched by Iran war as USS George Washington heads to the Mideast
items.summary: The five-month US war with Iran is straining the American carrier fleet, with the USS George Washington leaving the western Pacific to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East. The move leaves the Asia-Pacific temporarily without a US carrier, signalling a pivot of resources away from the region.

items.headline: Taliban mark five years in power amid what the UN calls a women's-rights crisis
items.summary: The Taliban marked five years since retaking Kabul, touting security and infrastructure gains while remaining internationally isolated. The UN women's agency described the ban on girls' secondary and higher education as the world's most severe women's-rights crisis, with millions of girls excluded from school.

items.headline: France's top court strikes down law banning under-15s from social media
items.summary: France's Constitutional Council struck down a law barring children under 15 from social media and phones in high schools, ruling it a disproportionate limit on freedom of expression. France was the first EU country to pass such a ban; President Macron vowed a legally robust version to take effect by 2027.

items.headline: Uber and Pony.ai to deploy more than 2,000 robotaxis across Europe
items.summary: Uber and China's Pony.ai expanded their partnership to put over 2,000 autonomous vehicles on European roads, growing from their existing Zagreb service into four more cities with Middle East deployment also planned. Pony.ai supplies the self-driving technology, Uber the ride-hailing platform, and local partners run the fleets.

items.headline: SanDisk's bullish outlook lifts Asian memory-chip stocks for a fifth day
items.summary: A strong AI-driven forecast from SanDisk pushed Asian memory names higher, with Kioxia rising as much as 8.7% in Tokyo and SK Hynix gaining 6.5% in Seoul. A Bloomberg gauge of Asian semiconductor stocks climbed as much as 1.6%, heading for a fifth straight daily advance.

items.headline: Apple trains its own China-only AI model with Alibaba in a first for a foreign firm
items.summary: Apple, working with Alibaba, has trained a proprietary large language model tailored for China and become the first foreign company cleared by Beijing to deploy its own AI model to mainland consumers. The system is set to power Apple Intelligence in China through an upcoming iOS update.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic cut model prices as cheaper Chinese rivals gain ground
items.summary: Facing customers testing lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Moonshot's Kimi, OpenAI and Anthropic both cut prices on flagship systems, with OpenAI reducing GPT-5.6 rates sharply and Anthropic pricing a new tier at roughly half its top model. Enterprises including DoorDash, Siemens and Airbnb are reported to be trialling the Chinese alternatives.

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway makes Alphabet a top-three holding with a roughly $17 billion bet
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's latest quarterly filing showed it added about 48 million Alphabet shares, lifting the stake to around $37.8 billion and making Google's parent one of its three largest positions. The conglomerate, now run by Greg Abel, also increased its Delta Air Lines and housing-related holdings.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs to buy ETF provider Neos for up to $2.25 billion
items.summary: Goldman Sachs agreed to acquire Neos Investments, which runs nearly two dozen options-based income ETFs with about $32 billion in assets, in a cash-and-equity deal worth up to $2.25 billion. It is Goldman's second niche-ETF purchase in under a year and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

items.headline: Maersk beats profit forecasts and lifts 2026 guidance as shares jump about 7%
items.summary: Shipping giant Maersk reported preliminary second-quarter underlying earnings of about $3 billion, well above the roughly $2 billion analysts expected, and raised its full-year guidance for the second time. Its shares rose 7% to 8% in Europe even as it warned of port and trucking bottlenecks from Red Sea and Hormuz rerouting.

items.headline: Oil climbs as US threatens an indefinite blockade of Iran's ports
items.summary: Brent crude rose 1.7% to $88.52 a barrel and US WTI gained 1.4% to $82.40 on Aug 14 after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of unprecedented measures and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington could hold an indefinite blockade of Iranian ports, following a reported Iranian attack on two ADNOC vessels.

items.headline: Wall Street eases from record as the small-cap Russell 2000 hits a fresh high
items.summary: US stocks slipped from Thursday's record on Aug 14, with the S&P 500 easing about 0.2% to near 7,785 after its first-ever close above 7,800, while the Dow fell around 108 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 set a fresh record and the S&P still logged a third straight weekly gain.

items.headline: 🏏 Manchester Super Giants reach The Hundred men's final, beating Sunrisers Leeds by 20 runs
items.summary: In the men's Eliminator at The Oval on Aug 14, Manchester Super Giants made 186 for 4 off 100 balls, powered by Paul Walter's 80 and Heinrich Klaasen's 63 off 26, then restricted Sunrisers Leeds to 166 for 7 as Josh Tongue took 4 for 26. They meet table-toppers Trent Rockets in the Lord's final.

items.headline: 🏏 Sunrisers Leeds edge Southern Brave to reach The Hundred women's final
items.summary: In the women's Eliminator in London on Aug 14, Southern Brave posted 114 for 7 and Sunrisers Leeds chased it down at 116 for 5 with 11 balls to spare. They will face Trent Rockets in the women's final at Lord's.

items.headline: 🎾 Tirante stuns an ailing Djokovic in the Cincinnati second round
items.summary: Argentina's Thiago Agustin Tirante beat world No. 3 Novak Djokovic 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the Cincinnati Open second round on Aug 15, the biggest win of his career. Djokovic, in his first match since Wimbledon, took the opening set but wilted in the heat, vomiting on court and taking a medical timeout in the 2hr 45min defeat.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 draws up 2027 calendar contingency plans amid Middle East conflict
items.summary: With the season in its summer break, F1 chief Stefano Domenicali said contingency plans are in place for the 2027 schedule if the US-Israel conflict with Iran, which forced the cancellation of the 2026 Bahrain and Saudi Arabian rounds, drags on. The sport will delay publishing next year's calendar until the autumn while still planning a full schedule.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen-to-a-rival talk for 2027 threatens to upend the driver market
items.summary: Summer-break reports of a possible Max Verstappen move for 2027, including chatter of a straight swap with McLaren's Oscar Piastri, have driven silly-season speculation that any switch would trigger a cascade of contract changes across the grid. Verstappen is also said to be weighing the direction of the 2027 engine rules.

items.headline: Rattlesnakes' own anti-venom proteins protect mice and point to human snakebite therapy
items.summary: Researchers led by Sean Carroll at the University of Maryland found that proteins in western diamondback rattlesnake blood, which help the snakes resist their own venom, kept mice alive after an otherwise lethal dose by staunching bleeding and blocking tissue damage. The work targets a snakebite crisis that kills up to 140,000 people a year.

items.headline: NASA's Perseverance rover watches Earth vanish behind the Martian moon Phobos
items.summary: A composite of seven Mastcam-Z images taken on July 2 shows Earth as a single point of light about 195 million miles away, then disappearing behind Phobos, the first time the feat has been captured from another planet's surface. Phobos crosses the Martian sky three times a day, making the alignment hard to catch.

items.headline: Estrogen-only hormone therapy is tied to lower dementia risk in a large study
items.summary: A Stanford Medicine analysis of 21,462 women found that estrogen-only menopausal hormone therapy was associated with 39% lower odds of dementia and 35% lower odds of Alzheimer's-related brain changes at autopsy. The researchers stressed the finding is an association, not proof of cause, and was published in the journal Neurology.

fun_fact.headline: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is larger than Earth
fun_fact.body: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a single storm so large that Earth could fit inside it. Astronomers have tracked it continuously for more than 150 years, winds at its edges exceed 400 kilometres per hour, and though it is the largest storm in the Solar System, it has been slowly shrinking for decades.

puzzle.title: The Cabin in the Field
puzzle.body: A hiker crests a ridge and finds a single cabin standing in the middle of a vast, empty field. Inside are 47 people, all dead. There is no sign of a struggle, no weapons, and nothing has been taken. The hiker understands what happened at a glance. What happened?
puzzle.approach: Question your assumptions about the everyday meaning of one key word in the setup.
puzzle.answer:
The 'cabin' is the cabin of an aircraft. The plane crashed in the field, killing all 47 people on board.
There was no struggle or weapon because it was a crash, not a crime, and nothing was taken because no one had been there to take it.

word_puzzle.title: Four Corners
word_puzzle.body:
KING · SALSA · THIMBLE · RANCH
WALTZ · ROOK · CAESAR · BOOT
QUEEN · ITALIAN · WHEELBARROW · TANGO
BISHOP · GREEK · IRON · SWING
word_puzzle.approach: Sort the 16 words into four groups of four. Watch for words that look like they belong in more than one group.
word_puzzle.answer:
Chess pieces: KING, QUEEN, ROOK, BISHOP
Dances: WALTZ, SALSA, TANGO, SWING
Monopoly tokens: THIMBLE, BOOT, WHEELBARROW, IRON
Salad dressings: RANCH, CAESAR, ITALIAN, GREEK

notes: Verification note: this run executed in a network environment where WebFetch/curl to news outlets was almost entirely egress-blocked and the WebSearch budget was exhausted. Items were cross-corroborated across multiple search-index results; deep links are the article URLs returned by search rather than click-verified pages, except the Global/Geopolitics section, whose AP links were confirmed against live AP article metadata.
Global section ran on AP (verified deep links). Singapore ran on Mothership. UK ran on BBC (primary).

India ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera): all primary Indian outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times) were unreachable for both search and fetch. Only the Modi Independence Day item carries a captured fallback deep link; the Arunachal floods and Women's Asia Cup items are corroborated but their deep links could not be captured (rendered without a link).

Below-floor sections due to source-reachability limits: India (3), UK (3), Other Miscellaneous News (3). A few items in India, UK, Tech and Misc are shown without a hyperlink because an allowed-outlet deep link could not be captured under the egress restrictions; they were multi-source corroborated.
3 retry-equivalent research passes were made per constrained section before accepting fewer items.
